title: You Need to Let Your Food Stick: How and When Sticking Can Build Flavor, Texture, and Structure
summary: America’s Test Kitchen host Lan Lam reframes the common assumption that sticking is universally bad by explaining how and why food sticks, when sticking is advantageous, and how cooks can control sticking with barriers, pan choice, and technique. The video covers (a) the mechanics of sticking at the protein–pan interface, (b) barrier strategies such as oil films and patinas on cast iron, (c) practical demonstrations including oven-baked French toast on a sprayed sheet, (d) the role of surfactant-containing cooking sprays to form thin, even barriers, (e) the use of fond to build pan sauces, and (f) specific demonstrations of sticking to shape texture—smashed burgers with lacy edges and a chiffon-based ice cream cake where sticking helps structure. The overarching message is balanced: don’t fear sticking in all cases, but recognize when it serves flavor, appearance, and ease of cooking, and when it should be minimized for cleanup or even browning objectives.
